newsitem.title: FRANCE: French scour Alps for mystery plane crash.
newsitem.headline: French scour Alps for mystery plane crash.

text.p: Rescue teams combed the hills around this French Alpine village on Thursday for a possible crashed plane after witnesses reported a mysterious fireball over the mountains.

Residents of the village of Dingy-St Clair, between Annecy and Thones in southeastern France and some 50 km (30 miles) from Geneva, told a Reuters television crew that they heard a plane noise and an explosion at dawn and saw a light in the sky.
Witnesses reported seeing the fireball over the mountains of Parleman about 10 km (six miles) east of Annecy at around five a.m. (0400 GMT).
Rescue work was hampered by bad weather which later cleared to allow two police helicopters to search the mountaintops. By early afternoon there still was no solution to the mystery, police said.
The owner of a local restaurant, Remond Dervaison, reported hearing the noise of a plane flying over the village.
Added an elderly village resident, Emma Panittet: "I heard a big bang noise and saw a blue light in the sky."
The village mayor, Monique Zurecki, said: "It probably was a small plane, perhaps a small military plane."
But airports and air traffic controllers in France and neighbouring Italy and Switzerland, baffled by speculation of a crash, said there were no reports of missing planes.

"We have no explanation," said a spokesman for the French aviation authority. He doubted a theory of a secret flight by a small private plane, saying: "To go flying at night in the mountains in a snowstorm would be to take a huge risk."
Air traffic controllers in Aix-en-Provence, who control air traffic over the south of France including international flights, said they had no reports of missing planes.
International flights are tracked on radar and none had disappeared from screens.
